newsitem.title: HONG KONG: IPO VIEW -- GITIC Enterprises IPO seen strong.
newsitem.headline: IPO VIEW -- GITIC Enterprises IPO seen strong.

text.p: The initial public offering (IPO) of Guangdong provinical government-backed GITIC Enterprises Ltd may receive the highest subscription rate among IPOs during the first half of 1997, analysts say.

Market sources expected the GITIC Enterprises' IPO to be about 500 to 600 times subscribed. The record so far this year is the IPO of GZI Transport Ltd, whose Hong Kong portion was 529 times subscribed.
Following that was Shum Yip Investment Ltd whose Hong Kong offering was 438 times subscribed.

Small issue size, the prospect of future assets injections, and its strong ties with its parent, one of the main financial institutions in China's southern province of Guangdong, were all selling points for GITIC Enterprises, analysts said.

"Certainly this IPO will receive an overwhelming response, extending the hot demand for red chips with an asset injection concept and strong ties with their parent," said Herbert Lau, analyst at Vickers Ballas.
GITIC Enterprises, a construction materials distributor, offered 100 million new shares at HK$1.05 each in its IPO, which will on March 20. Dealing in shares will begin on March 26.

Red chips, companies with close ties to China, have burst into action in Hong Kong recently. Investors are pushing their share prices higher, counting on the companies to raise funds and increase their assets.

Nikko Research Center said in a recent report that "red chips achieve exponential net profit growth via asset acquisitions and spin-offs...The earnings generated by the newly acquired assets are likely to secure profit growth."

The market was pushing red chips into asset purchases as investors needed an excuse to boost share prices, analysts said. "Basically what the public is doing is raising the price and saying: Here, I'll pay a bit more money for your stock, now will you inject?" said Charles de Trenck of UBS Securities.

GITIC Enterprises appears to have a strong asset injection concept because its parent is seen to be strong both financially and fundamentally, and could inject assets into the company to support its growth, analysts said.

The company is indirectly controlled by the Guangdong provincial goverment's investment arm, Guangdong International Trust and Investment Corp (GITIC Group), which had total assets of about 20 billion yuan ($2.4 billion) at the end of 1995.

"GITIC Group will give its full support to the development of our company (GITIC Enterprises), such as in the area of human resources and securing financial resources," Zhu Yiwen, vice chairman of GITIC Enterprises, said earlier this week.
GITIC Group engages in project financing, infrastructure and real estate development, industrial and hotel investment, securities trading, and import and export business.
Zhu was coy about asset injections by the parent.
"It (GITIC Group) does not have any immediate plan to inject assets or business into the company but we do not rule this possibility in future," Zhu said.

Nonetheless, analysts said they expected the parent to first inject construction materials and property related assets into the company, and possibly other businesses in the future, developing GITIC Enterprises into a conglomerate.
GITIC Enterprises imports and sells construction materials in Hong Kong and China, and also owns the second floor of a shopping mall at GITIC Plaza in Guangzhou.

The company said it would use the net proceeds of HK$90 ($12) million from the IPO to build and buy machinery for a processing plant in Guangdong province, and to expand its construction materials' distribution network in Hong Kong and China. ($ = 8.295 Chinese Yuan) ($ = 7.745 Hong Kong Dollars)
